items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: if Disney, because that's been Charlie Parker

ctx.x: but it really hadn't, but the general public. Now I always think that man, we can educate

the public to jazz. I said, yeah, I mean to bebop. We can educate them to bebop. Then I started thinking when I got older, I said that was some funny thinking. You know, like when you got a job doing something, you're not going there to teach, to educate the people to jazz. You're going there to make some money to play something that the people like to hear. So I called up all these old musicians and told them I was ready to play again. And I started playing. What did they say? Oh you're not playing any more…
But were there any clubs that you tried to do this bebop that you could get a gig? No. There weren't any. Okay. So there weren't any.

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: I said, if Disney, because that's been Charlie Parker, they didn't have a penny to spend for food. They could come to my house and eat.

ctx.x: was playing. But all three of us had teachers. Did you have a band with Clarence Ford?

Oh yeah, yeah. That's when I came out of the service. We had also created by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. I called all the old musicians up whom I played with and told them I didn't want to play with them no more. That's because the music you're playing is old, that's out of style. I'm playing bebop now. So Clarence Ford, we graduated from high school together. From Booker T. Washington? Yeah, same class. And Wilbur Hogan too. Did you have him? Yeah. Wilbur Hogan? Yeah. We graduated together. And he, what…
You were talking about Clarence Ford and you know how?
